subject: Deployment mode follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (Nova Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@novahealth.com>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@novahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (Nova Health)

Hi Sofia / Tom,

Great to meet you both today — thanks for walking through your current architecture and the migration goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Recap (from today's discovery):
- Current setup: mix of calls to OpenEndpoint API for prototyping + an in-house Triton cluster for heavy batch workloads.
- Key requirements: predictable latency for patient-facing features (~200ms p50 target), strict data residency for PHI, and a plan to reduce per-token cost for high-volume reporting jobs.
- Constraints: procurement timeline ~Q2, security questionnaires in progress, and a desire to avoid long re-architecture work right away.

Deployment mode guidance (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to get started (no infra to manage). Good for early integration and low-effort testing. Not ideal if you need strict VPC-only access or dedicated hardware SLAs.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit costs at scale. Good middle ground — supports private networking and SLAs, but still managed by Redwood. Recommended if you expect >50M tokens/month and need consistent latency for product traffic.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control over networking and keys; required for tightly regulated PHI scenarios or air-gapped deployments. Longer lead time for provisioning and potentially higher ops overhead.

Recommendation for Nova Health:
Given the PHI/residency needs and your latency targets, I recommend we scope a Dedicated capacity pilot scoped to the patient-facing endpoints + retain Hosted for internal testing/analytics in parallel. If procurement or compliance requires, we can evaluate a Private VPC deployment for the production cutover.

Next steps:
1) I'll attach a brief Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones (security sign-off, pilot provisioning, SLA review).
2) Can you share a rough monthly token estimate and expected peak concurrent requests for the patient-facing endpoint? That will let Rishi and Dev size Dedicated capacity.
3) If you want, I can schedule a 30-minute tech review with our infra team next week to walk through networking/VPC options.

Attachments: MAP_v1.pdf (one-page MAP)

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — very helpful summary. Quick answers and a couple follow-ups: 

- Token/traffic: ballpark today is ~12M tokens/month across analytics + internal tools; expected ramp to 600M/month if we move patient-facing features (~est. 2500 daily active users, ~3 calls / user).
- Peak concurrency: spikes up to ~120 concurrent inference calls during morning report window; typical p50 latency target for product is 200ms, p95 under 800ms.
- Data residency: production PHI must remain in our US region and ideally traverse only via customer VPC — this is a hard requirement.

We like the Dedicated pilot idea. A couple questions: 1) how long to stand up Dedicated with VPC peering? 2) Any migration assistance for model weights and prompts from our Triton pipelines?

We can do the tech review next Tuesday morning PT — Tom and I are available 9–11am PT.

Best,
Sofia Alvarez

Thanks Sofia — great detail, this is exactly what we needed. Quick answers inline and proposed meeting time.

1) Provisioning timeline: Dedicated with VPC peering typically ~7–10 business days once the MAP and security checklist are complete. We can speed up to ~5 days for a pilot if you approve an accelerated provisioning path.
2) Migration assistance: our Professional Services + infra team can help with model checkpoints and prompt templating. For Triton-style pipelines we usually:
   - validate model compatibility (quantized vs fp16)
   - convert checkpoints / provide a loader pattern for Redwood runtime
   - assist with KV cache and batching parameters to meet latency targets

Tech review: Tuesday 17 Feb, 10:00am PT works for our infra team — I'll send a calendar invite.

Rishi / Dev — can you give a ballpark Dedicated sizing and any concerns for a 600M tokens/month steady state with 120 peak concurrency and p50 target ~200ms? Also note requirement: all production traffic must exit via Nova's VPC (VPC peering / private link).

I've attached the MAP (MAP_v1.pdf) for reference.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: Dedicated sizing for Nova Health

Marissa / Rishi — quick sizing note based on the estimates:

Inputs we used: 600M tokens/month, 120 peak concurrent requests, model family assumed Llama-2-13B quantized fp16-ish runtime. Target p50 200ms (inference path only).

Ballpark Dedicated recommendation:
- 4 x A100-80GB (or equivalent H100/MI250 depending on availability) as baseline for the pilot.
- Autoscale policy: scale to 6 GPUs for sustained peaks >150 concurrent.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~700M tokens/month depending on batching efficiency and typical prompt length.
- Networking: support VPC peering + private link.

I'll drop a short capacity_estimate.xlsx with assumptions and ops notes. For migration: we can convert Triton checkpoints; we'll need a sample model checkpoint + 10 representative prompts to tune batching/caching params.

-dev
